segment.source: The Kerberos account is key material: it is shown to administrators, who hold dns.keys.
Set up the account of secure updates

Windows clients and domain controllers sign their dynamic updates with Kerberos. Tenko accepts them with the keys of one Active Directory computer account. Take over an account a domain administrator pre-staged with a one-time password (recommended: Tenko then owns and rotates its password), or import a keytab made with ktpass or msktutil.
Tenko never asks for a directory administrator's password.
The Active Directory domain in upper case, for example CORP.EXAMPLE.TEST.
One per line, host or host:port. Empty: found through the _kerberos._tcp records of the realm.
The computer account's name, 1 to 15 letters, digits or hyphens; the $ is added.
One per line: DNS/<name> for each Tenko node that is the primary of an AD zone, HTTP/<name> for Kerberos sign-in to the web UI.
The password the administrator set when creating the account. Tenko uses it once and replaces it at once.
1 to 365; 30 by default (TGL-32); 0 turns rotation off under the Lab profile only. Tenko keeps the previous key version until the tickets issued under it have expired.
The file ktpass or msktutil wrote. Tenko keeps the AES keys and not the file.
{file} is read; it is sent once with the import.
Needed when the keytab names only an SPN (ktpass /princ DNS/...).
Enter the realm as a domain name, for example CORP.EXAMPLE.TEST.
Each KDC is a host or host:port on a line of its own.
Enter at least one SPN, each DNS/<name> or HTTP/<name>.
The name is 1 to 15 letters, digits or hyphens.
Enter a number of days from 0 to 365.
A keytab is at most 1 MiB.

The administrator creates the account with the PowerShell block of the documentation ({section}) on a management host or a domain controller and types these values at its prompts. Tenko shows values only, never a script, and offers no copy: type them by hand.
The one you choose, as a distinguished name (OU=Service Accounts,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=test)
The block runs as a domain administrator and takes nothing Tenko wrote: each value is typed at its prompt and checked there, and anything pasted beyond one line is discarded.
Enter the one-time password of {name} in {realm}. Tenko changes it at once to one only it knows, stores the keys and runs the self-test.
The password stays the administrator's: Tenko does not rotate an imported account, and a password reset in Active Directory needs a new keytab.
The account is removed from Tenko
The administrator's: imported from a keytab
{negotiating} negotiating, {established} established, {refused} refused in the last hour

Tenko forgets the account's keys and stops accepting secure updates; zones with Kerberos settings fall back to their other lists. The account in Active Directory stays: a domain administrator deletes it there.

{reason, select, disabled {The account is disabled or locked in Active Directory. Enable it again.} keys_refused {The KDC refuses the keys Tenko holds: someone reset the account's password. Set a new one-time password and adopt the account again, or import a new keytab.} unknown {The account does not exist in the directory. Create it again with the PowerShell block and adopt it.} expired {The account's password has expired. Set a new one-time password and adopt the account again.} kdc_unreachable {No KDC answered. Check the KDCs listed, the _kerberos._tcp records and the network path to port 88.} adopt_incomplete {The adopt did not finish. Remove the account from Tenko, set a new one-time password and adopt it again.} change_pending {A password change is pending. Tenko asks the KDC again and commits or undoes it; run the self-test again in a few minutes.} kvno_not_newer {The KDC names a key version that is not newer than the ones Tenko holds. Check the account's msDS-KeyVersionNumber, then run the self-test again.} ticket_key {A ticket does not decrypt with the key Tenko holds for its version. Check that the SPN is on this account only (setspn -Q), or import a new keytab.} install_refused {The DNS role refused the keys. Check the SPNs of the account.} no_keys {Tenko holds no key for the account. Remove it from Tenko and adopt or import it again.} other {Check the account and the KDCs, then run the self-test again.}}
The KDC issues key version {kvno}, Tenko holds {held}
The password was changed outside Tenko, or the keytab was exported with another version. Adopt the account again with a new one-time password, or import a new keytab.
Add the SPN to the account on a domain controller: setspn -S {spn} with the account's name.
{spn} is held by another account as well
Find the other holder with setspn -Q {spn} and remove the SPN there.
The KDC does not issue AES tickets for the account
Tenko accepts AES only. Set msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes of the account to 24 (AES128 and AES256).
The clock is {skew} s off the KDC's
Synchronize the node's clock with the domain's time source (OPS-09). Kerberos refuses tickets beyond 300 s.
The password rotation failed ({failures} in a row)
The old keys stay current. Run the self-test: it names the cause, usually a disabled account or a password policy that refuses the change.
Read the detail below and run the self-test again.
